ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the circuit, the upper terminal of the voltage source Vs is connected to the left upper node, and the lower terminal is connected to the bottom common node; R2 is connected from the right output node to the bottom common node, and VL is marked across R2 with the upper terminal positive. R1 is connected between the left source upper node and the right output node, and is in parallel with an ideal diode. In the figure, the cathode of the diode is at the left source node, and the anode is at the right output node. Reasoning: Vs is a square wave with equal duty cycle, half a period is +8 V, half a period is -10 V, and R1 = R2 = 50 Ω. For the +8 V half-period, first assume the diode is off; then R1 and R2 form a voltage divider, VL = Vs·R2/(R1+R2) = 8×50/(50+50) = 4 V. At this time, the diode anode is at the output node at 4 V, and the cathode is at the source node at 8 V. The anode potential is lower than the cathode, so the diode is reverse-biased, and the off assumption holds; therefore VL = 4 V. For the -10 V half-period, if first assume the diode is off, voltage division gives VL = -10×50/(50+50) = -5 V. At this time, the diode anode is -5 V, and the cathode is -10 V. The anode potential is higher than the cathode, so the ideal diode conducts, equivalent to short-circuiting the source node and the output node; therefore VL = -10 V. The two levels each last T/2, so the average value is (4 + (-10))/2 = -3.0 V.

method.method_draft: First describe the image topology and diode orientation. For the +8 V half-cycle, tentatively take the diode open: the output is the divider value VL = Vs R2/(R1+R2) = 8/2 = 4 V. Since the diode anode is at the output node and the cathode is at the source node, 4 V is below 8 V, so the diode is reverse-biased; the off assumption is valid. For the -10 V half-cycle, the open-diode divider would give VL = -10/2 = -5 V. Now the anode at -5 V is above the cathode at -10 V, so the diode conducts and shorts the source-side and output nodes; hence VL = -10 V. With each level lasting T/2, compute the average as (4 + (-10))/2 = -3.0 V.
